transcript: In the Heights is finally back in New York thanks to this glorious new production at New York City Center. Now City Center is known for their star studded concert revivals, but for this production of in the Heights they've instead chosen to largely cast up and comers. Now if you are a theatre fan you will likely recognize some names like Tony Award winner Natalie Belcon as Abuela Claudia or Bad Cinderella herself Linedy Genao as Daniela. But you are also going to be introduced to a lot of performers that you probably have never heard of, all of whom are giving superb performances in this show. The vocals, the choreography, off the chart. The entire cast is really excellent. But just to shout out a few, Matt Martinez makes for an excellent Uznavi. He really makes the role completely his own, just oozes charisma. Another unexpected highlight was Ishmael Gonzalez as sonny, who despite having a very small role, really steals every single scene that they are in. And then there's also Jaci Calderon who plays Nina and has an absolutely gorgeous voice, and notably is going to be in Lin Manuel Miranda's the Warriors this spring, so she is definitely one to keep your eye on. But in the same way that the original in the Heights launched so many incredible careers, I would not be surprised if it's the same case for this production and this cast. And as with a lot of recent city center productions, despite Being a concert, this still basically feels like a fully staged production with just a slightly stripped back set. There is not a binder in sight, and it is really impressive what they are able to put together in just two weeks. Also shout out Justin Townsend who did the lighting. There is some really stunning lighting design here, especially the end of Act 1 and beginning of Act 2. But all in all, I was really happy to see that this was not just a copy and paste of the original production. There was so much effort made to really breathe new life into this show. from the overall direction, the performances, the design. And I think they were really successful at that. The show does still take place in 2008, which makes it officially a period piece, which makes me feel so old, but the show still feels just as fresh as it did back then. And this is going to be an easy Broadway Ben recommendation if you can even get tickets, because I'm pretty sure the whole runs basically sold out. But if you do have tickets, you are definitely in for a treat.
